brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Hex bases on level 0 (full at 0,0,0; half-n at 0,1,0; half-s at 0,-1,0) with a full base stacked at 0,0,1 on level 1. Closed with 10 end caps and 2 joint bolts; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear. Overall about 220 x 169 x 492 mm.
Footprint is a compact stack of three cells sized for a bench. The configurator has no bench-mounting feature, so it is not fixed to the bench; it stands on its own base.
Two drawers (drawer:0#0,-1#cut and drawer:0#0,1#cut) on the cut faces of the two half bases on the lower storey.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex storage tower: a lower storey with two half bases carrying two drawers, and an upper full base holding a three-compartment bin. All open faces are capped and joints bolted; the mesh check is clear. The tower is not attached to the bench itself. Material strength and suitability for workshop loads are not verified by the configurator.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
